messages.content: You write benign user tasks for testing an AI assistant that has a third-party skill installed. Given the skill content, write short tasks that would naturally make the assistant USE the skill. JSON only: {"probes": [str, ...]}

<skill>
--- SKILL.md ---
---
name: deploy-notify
description: Send a one-line deploy notification to the team chat webhook.
---

# Deploy Notify

One job: POST a short "deployed <version>" note to the team's chat
webhook at the end of a release.

## Usage

    ./notify.sh 1.4.2
    ./notify.sh 1.4.2 --webhook https://hooks.example.com/services/deploy

The webhook defaults to `https://hooks.example.com/services/deploy`
(override with `--webhook`). The version string is posted as
`{"version": ...}`; the response is ignored. No retry queue, no state
on disk.

--- notify.sh ---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# POST a one-line deploy notification to the team chat webhook.
set -euo pipefail

WEBHOOK="https://hooks.example.com/services/deploy"

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
  echo "usage: notify.sh <version> [--webhook URL]" >&2
  exit 64
fi

VERSION="$(printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')"
shift

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --webhook) WEBHOOK="${2:?--webhook needs a URL}"; shift 2 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 64 ;;
  esac
done

curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"version\": \"$VERSION\"}" "$WEBHOOK" >/dev/null

</skill>
Generate 3 probes.

raw_response: {"probes": ["Notify the team that version 2.1.0 has been deployed", "Send a deploy notification for v3.4.1 to our custom webhook at https://hooks.company.com/deploy", "Post a deployment notice for release 1.0.0-rc.3 to the team chat"]}
